_comment: Art and flavour manifest. Every buildable, recruitable and improvable thing in the game is keyed here by its id. NOTHING in the code hardcodes an icon or an image path - swap 'icon' for 'image' when real art arrives and no logic changes. 'blurb' is [GEN] placeholder prose and is the owner's to rewrite; the detail window derives every actual number from the data files, never from here.
_image: Optional. A path relative to the public/ directory, e.g. "art/buildings/barracks.png". When present it is drawn instead of the icon.

settlement_2.blurb: The village spreads beyond its first lane. New streets are laid, a market square is cleared, and the settlement is large enough to be called a town.

settlement_3.blurb: The town outgrows its bounds. Quarters form around the trades, the market becomes permanent, and the place begins to govern the country around it.

settlement_4.blurb: The city becomes the seat of the realm. There is only ever one, and everything a faction can build is unlocked here.

wooden_houses.blurb: Timber and thatch, packed close. Somewhere to put the people who keep arriving.

stone_houses.blurb: Stone walls and tiled roofs. They do not burn, and families stay in them for generations.

villas.blurb: Room to live rather than merely to shelter. The wealthy stop leaving for the countryside.

manors.blurb: Great houses for the people who own the country. The settlement's population grows fastest of all here.

wooden_palisade.blurb: A ditch and a ring of sharpened stakes. It will not stop an army, but it stops a raid.

stone_walls.blurb: Mortared stone, high enough to need ladders. The first fortification worth besieging.

city_walls.blurb: Curtain walls with towers, gates and a walkway. An attacker now needs a plan.

citadel.blurb: A fortress inside the walls. Even a fallen city can be held from here.

cottage_shops.blurb: Trades worked out of front rooms. Small money, but it arrives every month.

merchants.blurb: Traders with warehouses and contacts beyond the realm.

artisans.blurb: Skilled workshops making goods worth carrying a long way.

guildhouse.blurb: The trades organise, set their own prices, and pay the settlement handsomely for the privilege.

town_hall.blurb: Somewhere to keep the records and settle the disputes. People stay where they are governed - and the hall musters a militia of its own.

city_hall.blurb: Real administration: courts, charters and a treasury of its own.

palace.blurb: The seat of rule. The realm is administered from this room.

spear_quarters.blurb: Billets and a drill yard for spearmen. Unlocks Spear & Shield Infantry.

archery_range.blurb: Butts, bowyers and a long field. Unlocks Archers, and adds one to the settlement's defence.

axe_quarters.blurb: Quarters for shock troops who carry no shield. Unlocks Two-handed Sword and Axe.

barracks.blurb: Proper soldiers, properly housed. Unlocks Sword & Shield Infantry, and adds one to the settlement's defence.

stables.blurb: Horse lines, a farrier and pasture. Unlocks Light Cavalry, and adds one to the settlement's defence.

fishery.blurb: Boats, nets and a curing shed. Pays for every stretch of water around the settlement - which is what stops a coastal town being poorer than an inland one.

dock.blurb: A quay deep enough to tie up to. Unlocks Transports and Light Ships.

port.blurb: Cranes, bonded stores and a harbour master. Unlocks Heavy Ships.

shipyard.blurb: Slipways and a mast pond. Unlocks the Flagship.

farm.blurb: Ploughed strips worked from the settlement. Farms pay in gold, and plains double their yield.

mine.blurb: A shaft and a spoil heap. On a resource node it works that node; on ordinary ground it turns up both iron and stone.

sawmill.blurb: A saw pit and a timber yard. Wood is the scarcest thing in the game and this is nearly the only way to get it.

light_infantry.blurb: Levied men with whatever they own. Cheap, numerous, and the only thing a village can raise.

spear_infantry.blurb: A hedge of spears behind a shield wall. Twice as dangerous to cavalry, and hard for archers to hurt.

sword_infantry.blurb: Trained swordsmen with shields. The line that holds while everything else manoeuvres.

shock_infantry.blurb: Two hands on the weapon and no shield at all. Devastating on the charge, exposed to arrows.

skirmisher.blurb: Javelins and speed. Meant to harass and withdraw, not to hold ground.

archer.blurb: The longest reach in the roster. Ruinous against unshielded troops, helpless once reached.

light_cavalry.blurb: Fast riders for the flanks and the pursuit. Hits hard on the charge and does not stay to trade blows.

cavalry_archer.blurb: Shoots from the saddle and rides away. The hardest unit on the map to pin down.

heavy_cavalry.blurb: Armoured knights. The most expensive thing a faction can put in the field, and the most decisive.

transport.blurb: A hull for carrying men across water, not for fighting on it.

light_ship.blurb: Fast and cheap. Enough to chase a transport, not enough to face a warship.

heavy_ship.blurb: A real warship, built to win a sea fight rather than to survive one.

flagship.blurb: The pride of a realm's navy, and a national project in timber alone.
